title: Sparse attention trace and SM-idle clustering - Sep 2026
content:
Purpose:
Notes from an ad-hoc profiling run focused on a sparse-attention variant (custom kernel + fallback dense path) that is showing elevated SM idle waves on A100 instances. Goal is to capture the constellation of events that lead to idle clusters, identify whether latency spikes are coming from serialization at kernel boundaries (cudaGraph replay / stream synchronization) or from load imbalance inside the sparse kernel itself, and propose short experiments to isolate cause and mitigation paths.

Context / why we care:
- Sparse attention reduces compute for long contexts but can introduce highly-variable per-block workloads (irregular memory access, dynamic row lengths).
- In production workload (chat endpoint with pinned KV cache + prefix caching) we see 99th percentile token latency regressions on certain request mixes despite average throughput improvement.
- Hypothesis: kernel-level imbalance + suboptimal stream/graph replay ordering causes microscale SM idle waves that amplify under bursty arrival patterns.

Test setup (how traces were collected):
- HW: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100), CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.2, NVIDIA Nsight Systems 2026.2.1 snapshot captures.
- Binary: serving-runtime:perf/sparse-kernel-experiment:commit 3f7a2b (custom sparse kernel + fallback).
- Workload: synthetic mix (60% small prompts, 40% long prompts with sparsity mask). Token lengths 8-2048, arrival poisson bursts.
- Recording: 2x Nsight timeline captures (full system + per-process nvtx markers) + cudaGraph capture enabled for steady-state window. Also collected per-kernel CUPTI counters: active_warps_per_sm, achieved_occupancy, l2_hit_rate, shared_load_utilization.
- Not instrumented: persistent kernel variant (we used transient).

Observed signals (raw impressions from timeline):
- Periodic SM-idle bands spanning ~3-8ms every ~40ms during burst windows. In timeline view these correlate with gaps between the sparse kernel launch and subsequent small dense fallback kernels.
- CUDA graph replay segments show serialized host-side API calls because the graph contains both sparse and dense variants with conditional branching implemented via host control flow (graph recorded per-inference). The replay timeline shows short (~50-200us) gaps between kernel launches that align with SM idle ramps down/up.
- Sparse kernel itself shows load imbalance: about 20% of warps finish earlier and stall on a shared synchronization point (per-block dynamic loops). Achieved occupancy per SM displayed high variance (0.25 - 0.9) across time slices.
- L2 miss bursts coincide with sparse kernel's gather stage; when mask density is very low we see tensor cores underutilized and memory stalls increase.

Quantitative snippets from counters (summary):
- Mean achieved_occupancy (sparse kernel): 0.62, std 0.18.
- Active_warps_per_sm drop during idle bands from ~24 -> ~3 (A100 theoretical max 64 warps?).
- Kernel launch latency (host observable): dense fallback kernels have 0.12ms nominal latency, but during graph replay windows they show up after 0.3-0.6ms delay (accounting for host queuing + serial work).

Hypotheses / root cause candidates:
1) Host-side serialization during cudaGraph replay when graphs are re-recorded per-request because of branchy sparse/dense mixture. This leads to micro-gaps between kernels that permit SMs to ramp down and create idle waves.
2) Irregular per-block work inside sparse kernel causing intra-kernel imbalance and syncthreads-like stalls at dynamic loop boundaries. Some blocks finish quickly and later blocks dominate, leaving whole-SM idle tails.
3) Memory subsystem pressure (gather scatter) causing L2/back-end stalls which, combined with the above, exacerbates perceived idle time in the timeline.

Short experiments to disambiguate (ordered cheap -> more invasive):
A) Force single-path recording: create two static cudaGraphs (one sparse-heavy, one dense-heavy) and route requests at dispatch-time without re-recording. If idle bands disappear, host re-recording is likely a major contributor. (Low effort, config-level change).
B) Convert sparse kernel to persistent-thread model for hot paths (avoid per-launch overhead and keep warps resident). Look for reduction in SM-idle bands and improvement in occupancy variance. (Medium effort).
C) Introduce coarse-grained intra-kernel load balancing: bucket row lengths and process largest-first across blocks; or use cooperative groups to redistribute leftover work. Measure reduction in per-SM variance. (High effort).
D) Microbenchmark gather pattern under synthetic low-density masks to measure L2 miss amplification and TLB churn. If memory stalls dominate, try prefetching or reorganizing data layout. (Low-medium).

Immediate next steps / action items (owners):
- Aisha: implement A) static graph path + replay test in perf harness, collect Nsight timeline for same synthetic bursts (due: 2026-09-18).
- Marcus: add a simple persistent-thread prototype for sparse kernel, a single launch variant to compare occupancy metrics (due: 2026-09-24).
- Diego: craft microbenchmark for gather scatter and run L2/TLB counters (due: 2026-09-20).
- Add a Jira ticket (SERV-1589) to track follow-ups and link to PRs.

Notes / heuristics learned during capture:
- NVTX markers inserted at host-level (enqueue, graph-record-start, graph-replay-start) were essential; lacking them the timeline gaps are ambiguous. Recommend standardizing NVTX spans for all graph record/replay points.
- Use Nsight filter to ‘group by SM activity’ to more quickly highlight idle wave patterns; exporting CSV of per-kernel achieved_occupancy made statistical comparison trivial.
- Watch out for host-side memcpy operations that can interleave with graph replay; in our traces small cudaMemcpyAsync calls queued on the same stream were occasionally serialized.

Open questions:
- Do we see the same patterns on H100 (different scheduling/wave occupancy)? Need cross-gen comparison.
- For production request mixes, what fraction of calls actually hit the sparse path vs fallback? This meta-distribution affects global scheduling decisions.

Appendix: quick links to artifacts from this run
- Nsight capture files: gs://redwood-perf/sparse-trace/sep14-capture-1.nsys (internal)
- Perf harness config: github PR (linked_artifacts above)
- Quick script to export occupancy CSV: scripts/occupancy/export_occupancy_csv.py (in perf repo)

Rough conclusion (working):
Both host-side graph re-recording and intrinsic sparse kernel imbalance appear to contribute. Cheap wins: avoid per-request graph re-recording (static graphs + dispatch) and add NVTX markers across record/replay boundaries. Medium-term: persistent-thread kernel and intra-kernel load balancing are promising but require prototyping to evaluate correctness/perf tradeoffs.
